sources.evidence_excerpt: Version 4.42 lint commands with no input returned zero; the sibling test command failed closed.

intended_control: Lint configuration or template files and fail when the invocation names no files to inspect.
false_acceptance: Both lint entry points returned success with no inputs, allowing a mistyped invocation to certify an empty set.

causal_chain.claim: The help text presents linting as a file-checking command whose status reports detected errors.
Calling lint or template lint with no file arguments returned zero.
The sibling test command reported no tests and returned one, demonstrating an available fail-closed convention.
The lint success signal does not distinguish an empty invocation from a non-empty clean run.

steps: Run the redpandadata/connect:4.42 container with template lint and no file argument.
Repeat with lint and no file argument.
Compare both statuses with the test command when no tests are found.
reproducer.observed: Both lint commands returned zero without inspecting a file; the no-tests command returned one.
reproducer.expected: A lint invocation with no files should diagnose the empty scope and return non-zero.

facts: The issue includes versioned container commands, help text, and exit statuses.
derivations: The examples make a missing positional argument easy to confuse with a legitimate empty invocation.
unknowns: No maintainer response or fixing change defines whether zero-input lint was intentionally supported.

counterclassification.label: OUT_OF_SCOPE
counterclassification.would_be_primary_if: Zero-input lint is explicitly documented as a valid no-op whose success makes no claim that files were checked.
